> LLM-generated review from https://github.com/canonical/maas-code-reviewer.
> Intended to assist a human reviewer, not replace one — suggestions may be
> incorrect, please verify before acting.


The approach matches LP:2171421 (verified on Launchpad: rate/connection limiting shipped with active defaults in 3.7.4 and is not gated on hardening) and reuses the convention already established by the BIND9 hardening options ('0 means: use the hardening default'), with templates correctly guarding the whole block on a non-empty api_rate_limit_rate, so an empty rate cleanly disables both directives. Tests cover the three main paths on both services. Two real issues: (1) the rack-side options still use formencode's Number, which accepts fractional values (verified: Number.to_python('10.5') == 10.5), so the commit body's claim that 'both are validated with Int so a fractional value cannot reach the NGINX config' is only true on the region side — a fractional burst/conn in rackd.conf renders as 'burst=20.5'/'limit_conn api_conn 20.5', which nginx rejects and leaves the rack proxy unable to reload; (2) the commit body says unset (rather than 0) is the sentinel so that a burst of 0 stays configurable, but the implementation uses if_missing=0 plus a falsy 'or' fallback, making explicit 0 indistinguishable from unset, so nginx's burst=0 (reject excess instead of queueing) is unreachable. Also one contradictory sentence in the docs. Minor note for the changelog: deployments that previously wrote api_rate_limit_rate=20r/s explicitly keep limiting after upgrade; only truly absent keys flip to off.

src/provisioningserver/config.py.902: formencode's Number accepts fractional values (Number.to_python('10.5') == 10.5, and min=0 passes), so api_rate_limit_burst: 20.5 (or an unquoted YAML float) validates here and interpolates into rackd.nginx.conf.template as 'burst=20.5 nodelay;' / 'limit_conn api_conn 20.5' (see line 908 for api_conn_limit), which nginx rejects — nginx -t fails and the rack proxy can't reload. The commit message claims Int validation prevents fractional values reaching the NGINX config; that's only true on the region side (src/maasserver/config.py:335 uses formencode Int, which rejects the string form and truncates floats). Please use Int (from formencode.validators, already imported in this module) for both options.

src/maasserver/regiondservices/http.py.140: The 'or' fallback conflates an explicit 0 with unset: RegionConfiguration.api_rate_limit_burst has if_missing=0 (src/maasserver/config.py:335) and 0 is falsy, so 'api_rate_limit_burst: 0' always renders as burst=60. The change description states unset (rather than 0) is the sentinel precisely so that burst=0 (reject excess requests instead of queueing them under nodelay) stays configurable — that goal isn't met, and the help text now actively documents '0 means: use the default (60)'. Either implement a real unset sentinel (if_missing=None works — ConfigurationOption.__get__ returns validator.if_missing verbatim when the key is absent — and check 'is None' here and in rackdservices/http.py) or correct the commit body; as written the behavior contradicts the stated intent.

src/provisioningserver/rackdservices/htt.255: Same conflation as the region side: ClusterConfiguration.api_rate_limit_burst defaults to 0 when unset and 0 is falsy, so an explicit burst of 0 (nginx semantics: reject excess requests instead of queueing) is silently replaced with 60. The commit message claims 'Unset (rather than 0) is used ... so a burst of 0 stays configurable'; use a None sentinel with 'is None' checks (or mirror whatever fix lands on the region side) so explicit 0 survives, otherwise update the option help text and commit body to match this behavior.

docs/reference/configuration-guides/secu.264: 'leaving it empty turns off both rate and connection limiting' is only true when hardening is inactive. When hardening is active, an empty api_rate_limit_rate falls back to the hardening default 20r/s and limiting stays on (see the option help in src/maasserver/config.py and the 'or' fallback in regiondservices/http.py:125). Reword, e.g. 'leaving it empty disables limiting on non-hardened deployments; on hardened deployments it falls back to the hardening default (20r/s).'
